analysis.title: MS Savone - Global Reflections 14 Nov 2026
key_insights: Sales commentary (not research). Investors are rebuilding exposure slowly with low conviction. US equities snapped a four-week losing streak, but the rebound has done more for prices than for conviction.
With 91% of S&P 500 companies reported, earnings broadly met a high bar. Beats were more typical after two stronger quarters.
US L/S net exposure is 47%, the 5th percentile over 12 months. Gross is 202%, a one-year trough. Buying was split roughly evenly between long additions and short covering.

US 2Y yields rose ~37bps over the week after firm inflation and hawkish Fedspeak. Friday morning pricing implied ~3.5 hikes by September 2027, versus an MS base case of 25bps moves in December and March, with January a risk.
The S&P 500 12-month forward P/E fell from 23.2x in 4Q25 to 18.2x. Savone and the MS Europe team argue this already reflects the hawkish Fed shift.

AI Adopters have outperformed Enablers by ~26pts since end-September, yet earnings revisions still favor Enablers. Hyperscalers have issued $67B of debt since 9/30, and credit is differentiating between hyperscalers and riskier data-center/neocloud borrowers.

CoreWeave beat on revenue and adjusted operating income, raised guidance and added >900MW of contracted power QoQ. About $9B of prepayments and existing IG/enterprise contracts cover 75% of planned 2027 capex, but financing facilities still need to close.

Cisco raised FY27 AI infrastructure revenue outlook from hyperscalers to $9B from $7.5B. Cerebras announced a cloud deal with a top-three hyperscaler. Nebius guided revenue toward the low end of its range after third-party capacity delays.

MS thematic research (Byrd, Nowak) calls the post-midterm AI selloff an overreaction. New Texas and Ohio regulation is expected to move ~5GW of US data center projects from 2028 to 2029. Hyperscaler capex forecasts are unchanged at $1.6T in 2027 and $1.8T in 2028. US data center additions are seen falling 4% YoY in 2028 and rising 38% in 2029.

Mike Wilson sees the correction entering its final phase and expects a retest of last week's lows before a possible year-end rebound. Semiconductors are down roughly 40% since June. 2027 capex is 5% of S&P 500 consensus revenue, and 44% of index companies now quantify AI benefits.

Michael Gapen: October CPI rose 0.4% headline and 0.3% core MoM. He raised October core PCE to 0.35% MoM from 0.22%. He expects 25bps hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.50%, with January a risk (4.50-4.75% terminal). A 50bps December move needs renewed oil pressure and clear labor overheating.

Europe: STOXX 600 closed at a record after a ~2.6% weekly gain, its best week since June. The DAX also hit a record. A >3% Euro Stoxx 50 week alongside a >25bps rise in US 10Y yields has happened only 13 times since 2000. Q3 EPS growth is tracking ~28%.

Macro systematic strategies sold ~$230B of equities globally over the past month and could have ~$20B of US equity supply left next week. Estimates point to ~$60B of potential equity demand over the next month if realized vol falls to 15%. Single-name realized vol is at the 99th percentile of its five-year history.
Retail net bought $1.6B of NVDA on Thursday per QDS models, nearly 10x the next-most-bought name. Retail bought ~$25B overall over the week through Thursday.
NVDA had its biggest ever market cap decline and trades on sub-12x 12M forward earnings, the lowest P/E in 13 years, with earnings next week.
Korea: MS sees corporate ROE rising from ~8% toward 14%+ by 2030 and payouts from 35-40% to 50-60%. Overweight names are SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, Hyundai Motor and KB Financial.

Retail: specialty retailers and department stores have rallied ~25% from September lows, driven more by multiple expansion than earnings revisions. MS expects ~80% of companies to deliver in-line or better 3Q26 results.
Corporate credit (Sheets): the factor selloff is a clearing event, not the end of the cycle. Oil is 17% below end-October levels.
Next week's calendar: retail sales, Fed minutes, consumer sentiment, the MS Asia Pacific Summit in Singapore, and NVDA, PANW and WMT earnings (10% of market cap still to report).

sector_views.rationale: Gutman and Pauker see the rotation having a next leg for names with recovering demand. Straton cautions the ~25% rally since September has been multiple-driven.
Wilson says the ~40% decline since June is nearing its end, but selectivity remains critical.
Kim sees the main concern as a '2028 earnings cliff' narrative, not delayed data center builds, and makes Samsung a Top Pick.
Cohen expects further pricing declines at the January renewals, with loosening terms signaling sustained pressure.
Eddy Wang says growth is running out and competition may consume the 'maturity dividend'.
Ravi Shanker's AlphaWise survey points to ~5% corporate travel budget growth in 2026 and 2027 and ~4% passenger volume growth in 2027.
Pulleyn prefers large caps for index weight, liquidity and diversified growth.
Seok and Oh expect ROE to rise toward 14%+ by 2030 and payouts to rise to 50-60%.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave (CRWV): beat on revenue and adjusted operating income and raised guidance, per Savone. No figures given for the beat. Reported this week.
Cisco (CSCO): raised FY27 AI infrastructure revenue outlook from hyperscalers to $9B from $7.5B. Reported this week.
Nebius (NBIS): guided revenue toward the low end of its range after third-party capacity delays. Reported this week.
Siemens Energy: higher long-term targets and EUR15B of annual FCF guided for 2028-30. Burberry: profitability beat. Infineon: AI data-center demand approaching EUR4B in FY27. All reported this week.
S&P 500: 91% of companies have reported. Earnings met a high bar, with more typical beats after two stronger quarters. Europe Q3 EPS growth is tracking ~28%.

Retail 3Q26 preview (Straton): MS expects ~80% of companies to deliver in-line or better results and ~90% to reiterate or raise guidance. Macy's has EPS upside and a likely guidance raise. URBN and VSXY are positioned to beat and raise. AEO and GAP face downside risk. KSS could disappoint.
Upcoming next week: NVDA, PANW and WMT report, with ~10% of market cap left to report. NVDA trades on sub-12x 12M forward earnings.
Unity (U): ~80% incremental EBITDA margins YTD after 3Q, per Matt Cost.
Seagate (STX): shares trade at 5x Woodring's CY28 EPS, ~3x his bull case. Buybacks could reach ~30% of market cap in 2.5 years.

Housing weakness, with home sales the worst since 2010.

vol_and_positioning: US L/S net leverage is 47% (24th percentile since 2010, 5th over 1Y). Gross is 202% (86th since 2010, 1st over 1Y).
European gross leverage rose 1ppt to 175% (71st percentile over 1Y). Asia gross leverage held at 124% (2nd percentile over 1Y).
Single-name realized volatility is at the 99th percentile of its five-year history.
Macro systematic strategies have ~$20B of US equity supply left next week. ~$60B of demand is possible if 1-week, 2-week and 1-month realized vol fall to 15%.
CTAs are projected to buy ~$3B a day in Europe over the next week. The gap to cycle highs is ~$200B.
November MTD: Americas L/S +0.5% vs S&P +0.2%. Europe L/S +0.6% vs EURO STOXX 600 +2.7%. Asia L/S -0.8% vs MSCI Asia Pacific -1.7%.
Retail bought ~$25B over the week through Thursday, including $1.6B of NVDA on Thursday.
Funds unwound shorts into strength and sold longs into weakness in the US. Seasonal trends point to gross unwinding.

France 2027 budget negotiations and the 2027 presidential election.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P 500 forward P/E has fallen from 23.2x to 18.2x, which MS says already reflects the hawkish Fed shift, and positioning is light.
tension_points.bear_case: Futures price ~3.5 hikes by September 2027 against an MS base case of two 25bps hikes, and Gapen says a hot jobs and inflation round could add a January hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another firm jobs and inflation round, which Gapen says could trigger a January hike, or renewed oil pressure with labor-market overheating, which could bring a 50bps December move.

tension_points.bull_case: Byrd and Nowak say the selloff is an overreaction, with ~5GW delayed from 2028 to 2029 and capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6T for 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: US data center additions fall 4% YoY in 2028, permitting restrictions could widen after the Democratic midterm sweep, and financing facilities for neoclouds still need to close.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Permitting restrictions that go beyond the 2028 to 2029 push-out, or neocloud financing facilities failing to close.

tension_points.bull_case: Adopters have outperformed Enablers by ~26pts since end-September, and 44% of S&P 500 companies now quantify AI benefits.
tension_points.bear_case: Earnings revisions still favor Enablers, suggesting price has moved ahead of fundamentals.

tension_points.bull_case: Discretionary stocks remain near relative performance lows and ~80% of companies are expected to deliver in-line or better 3Q26 results.
tension_points.bear_case: The ~25% rally since September lows was driven more by multiple expansion than earnings revisions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 3Q26 results or guidance that fall short of elevated expectations, as Straton flags for KSS, AEO and GAP.
